newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lyonnaise des Eaux/Suez merger terms set - source.
newsitem.headline: Lyonnaise des Eaux/Suez merger terms set - source.

text.p: The merger between financial holding Cie de Suez and utility Lyonnaise des Eaux will use a parity of 41 Suez shares for 20 Lyonnaise stock, a source close to the deal said on Thursday.

The source told Reuters that Suez would make a dividend payment of "23.60 or 24.60 francs" per share, which includes both a normal payment and a special payment, and compares with a 1995 dividend of 8.20 francs ($1.41).
This would lead to a total dividend payment of between 3.6 and 3.8 billion francs.
The source added that Suez would hold on to its remaining financial assets in the short term. "The idea is to create a services group," the source said.
"But in a later stage, between one, one-and-a-half and five years, the group will sell peripheral assets," he said.
"It would be a mistake to stop offering financial services to private individuals," he added, saying there were no plans to sell the Sofinco bank, as some analysts had speculated.

Lyonnaise and Suez will on Friday unveil the terms of their merger which will create a group with a market value of 75 billion francs at Thursday's share prices, and with over 150 billion francs in sales.
Financial analysts said they expected Suez to sell Sofinco, a bank specialising in consumer credit. Credit Agricole has an option to buy 20 percent of the bank from 1998.
These analysts believe it best for the old Suez, founded in 1858 to finance the Suez canal, to "disappear" with the cash being channelled to Lyonnaise des Eaux activities in water and communication.
One analyst estimated Suez could generate between 15 and 20 billion francs by selling its assets in the financial sector.

Jean-Louis Beffa, chairman of Cie de Saint-Gobain and a Suez shareholder who asked for a special dividend payment, has said that two-thirds of the Suez portfolio is made up of financial assets that would not fit in the new group.
The source also said the Belgian authorities, who feared French interests would become too powerful in the gas and electricity group Tractebel SA, had now been reassured.
In fact, the stake of Societe Generale de Belgique SA in Tractebel will drop to 50.03 percent from 65 percent after Tractebel's planned merger with Powerfin SA. ($ = 5.797 French Francs)
